problem_motivation.content: Developing large-area THGEM foils is necessary to realize a THGEM-based muography system.
problem_motivation.evidence_span: In order to realize a muography system based on THGEM technology, the development of large-area detector foils is a critical requirement.

prior_approach.content: Muon tomography infers internal density variations using naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Muon tomography, often termed as muography, exploits this property to infer on internal density variations in large or shielded structures without using artificial radiation sources.

prior_approach.content: Early muon absorption measurements, especially Alvarez's pyramid study, established transmission muography.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The historical origin of muon tomography or muography is often traced back to early absorp- tion measurements for overburden studies and, most notably, to the pioneering work by Alvarez and collaborators who used cosmic muon absorption to search for hidden chambers in the Pyramid of Khafre [1].

prior_approach.content: Transmission muography measures directional attenuation relative to open-sky flux to reconstruct opacity.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In transmission (attenuation) muography, one measures the directional reduction of muon flux through a target relative to open-sky expectations and reconstructs the integrated density (“opacity”) along each line of sight.

prior_approach.content: Scattering muography uses muon angular deflection from multiple Coulomb scattering.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A second major class is scattering muography, which uses the angular deflection of muons caused by multiple-Coulomb-scattering (MCS) as they traverse matter [6].

prior_approach.content: Various detector technologies have previously been explored for muography.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Consequently, a wide range of detector technologies were explored for muography, including plastic scintilla- tors [11, 12], drift tubes and drift chambers [13, 14], resistive plate chambers (RPCs) [15–17], nuclear emulsions [18], and micro-pattern gaseous detectors (MPGDs) [19–22].

prior_approach.content: Prior studies systematically examined how THGEM geometry affects gain, stability, and discharge probability.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Systematic studies have been carried out to investigate the dependence of gain, stability, and discharge probability on geometrical parameters such as hole diameter, pitch, sub- strate thickness, and rim etching [26, 27].

prior_approach.content: Prior work also studied charging-up, gain uniformity, and long-term stability under irradiation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The effects of charging-up [31], gain uniformity [32], and long-term stability under sustained irradiation have also been examined, providing important insights into operational behavior relevant for prolonged data-taking scenarios.

prior_approach.content: THGEM operation has previously been demonstrated across multiple gas mixtures and pressures.
prior_approach.evidence_span: THGEM operation has been demonstrated in a variety of gas mixtures and pressures, highlighting the flexibility of the technology and its adaptability to different experimental conditions [33, 34].

prior_approach.content: Early THGEM spatial-resolution studies focused on charge transport, avalanche development, and signal formation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Early studies of THGEM spatial performance primarily focused on charge transport, avalanche development, and signal formation

prior_approach.content: This work continues the authors' earlier THGEM study.
prior_approach.evidence_span: in collaboration with a few local industries as a continuation of our earlier study [26].

prior_approach.content: The fabricated THGEM variants were characterized by gas gain after multiple foil-conditioning techniques.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The prototypes built with the fabricated variants of the THGEM foil underwent rigorous characterization by studying their gas gain, following the application of multiple conditioning techniques to the foils.

prior_approach.content: The selected prototype was further evaluated in two gas mixtures and in single- and double-stage operation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: On the basis of performance, one of the prototypes was opted for further investigations and subjected to extensive performance evaluation with two different gas mixtures. The key requisites for muon detectors in a muography setup, the muon detection efficiency and the position resolution of the prototype were investigated using both the single and the double-stage configuration to examine the suitability of multi-stage operation.

rejected_alternative.content: Conventional thin GEM foils are implicitly disfavored in favor of THGEMs because THGEMs are more robust and easier to handle for large-scale or field use.
rejected_alternative.evidence_span: Compared to conventional thin GEM foils, THGEMs offer enhanced mechanical robustness, simplified handling, and greater tolerance to imperfections, all of which are advantageous for detectors intended for large-scale or field-deployable systems [25].

inspiration_source.content: THGEM was developed based on the GEM concept introduced by Sauli.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: Initially inspired by the concept of GEM, introduced by F. Sauli in 1997 [23], THGEMs have been developed to enhance mechanical stability and simplify man- ufacturing, without compromising performance [24].

inspiration_source.content: The polishing and cleaning protocol was initially based on a method reported in reference 39.
inspiration_source.evidence_span: The polishing and cleaning procedures applied to the THGEMs were initially inspired by the methodology reported in [39], and subsequently refined through the implementation of modified approaches developed in this work.

causal_claim.content: Greater scattering in dense or high-Z materials gives scattering muography better sensitivity to compact high-Z objects behind lower-Z shielding.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Since scattering depends on radiation length and is more pronounced for dense/high-Z materials, scattering muography provides enhanced sensitivity to compact high-Z objects even when they are shielded by lower-Z materials, making it attractive for security screening and safeguards [7, 8].

causal_claim.content: Fine granularity, flexible geometry, and modern electronics compatibility have driven increased interest in MPGDs.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Among these, MPGDs have attracted increasing attention due to their fine granularity, flexible detector geometry, and compatibility with modern readout electronics.

causal_claim.content: Excellent tracking performance in other applications motivated consideration of GEMs and Micromegas for muography.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Micromegas have demonstrated excellent tracking performance in high-energy physics and related applications, motivating their consideration for muography systems.

causal_claim.content: Conditioning stabilizes THGEM operation and suppresses micro-discharges while improving long-term gain stability.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These conditioning procedures play a crucial role in stabilizing detector operation by removing trapped moisture, cleaning residues and reducing surface asperities which in turn help to suppress micro-discharges and improve long-term gain stability.

causal_claim.content: A best-performing foil was selected based on measured gains over different electric-field configurations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: On the basis of measured gains over a range of electric-field configurations, the prototype with the best-performing foil was subjected to further investigations.

causal_claim.content: Etched rims were used to reduce electrical discharges caused by high applied voltages on THGEM surfaces.
causal_claim.evidence_span: To mitigate the occurrence of electrical discharges caused by high voltages, applied to the conducting surfaces on either sides of the THGEM foil, rims of widths 50 and 100 𝜇m were etched around each hole through standard chemical processes.

causal_claim.content: Phase-II polishing/cleaning was used to reduce discharge probability and enable reaching the Paschen limit.
causal_claim.evidence_span: To reduce the discharge probability and achieve the Paschen limit, a systematic polishing and cleaning procedure for those two THGEM foils (A, and C) was adopted in phase-II.

causal_claim.content: Removing the ENIG finish caused surface oxidation on bare copper during high-temperature baking.
causal_claim.evidence_span: The ENIG surface-finish, originally applied by the manufacturer, was removed during the polishing of the foils in phase-II. As a result, some surface oxidation occurred on the bare copper electrodes during high-temperature baking due to exposure to the atmosphere

causal_claim.content: Extending the operating regime after phase-II enabled a three-fold gain enhancement.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, three-fold enhancement in the gain value could be achieved.

causal_claim.content: Operating gas choice affects amplification, stability, and spatial resolution.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Since the choice of operating gas significantly impacts charge amplification, operational stability, and spatial resolution, the detector performance was studied using two different Argon-based gas mixtures at atmospheric pressure

causal_claim.content: Charging-up caused gain to flatten at higher voltages.
causal_claim.evidence_span: This behaviour was influenced by charging-up of the THGEM foil, which eventually led to a stooping trend in the gain at higher voltages.

causal_claim.content: THGEM-B was selected as optimal because it operated at lower voltage.
causal_claim.evidence_span: On the basis of the gain study of the three THGEM prototypes, the THGEM-B prototype was considered as the optimal choice owing to its lower operating regime

causal_claim.content: Increasing drift field first raised gain, then reduced it above about 2.5 kV/cm.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As can be noted from figure 11a, the gain in both of the gas mixtures increased with the rise in drift field to reach a maximum value, and eventually, decreased at higher drift field values above 2.5 kV/cm.

causal_claim.content: Increasing induction field raised gain rapidly at low values.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Figure 11b shows that the gain increased rapidly at low induction fields

causal_claim.content: Ar-isobutane was judged better than Ar-CO2 because it gives lower working voltage, fewer charging-up issues, and higher gain.
causal_claim.evidence_span: By comparing the detector performance with both the Ar-based mixtures, it can be inferred that the Ar-isobutane (95:5) is a better choice as it offers a working voltage regime lower than that of Ar-CO2 (90:10) facilitating safe operation with less charging-up issue, and achieves better gain.

causal_claim.content: Average hit multiplicity increased with detector gain, especially in double-stage Ar-isobutane at high gain.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It shows that that the multiplicity increases with the gain and for the double-stage configuration, a fairly large multiplicity can be observed with Ar-isobutane (95:5) at higher gain.

causal_claim.content: In single-stage operation, position resolution improved as gain increased.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In case of single-stage THGEM operation using Ar–CO2 (90:10), a clear improvement was observed with increase in the detector gain.

causal_claim.content: At low drift field, spatial resolution is worse; increasing drift field improves resolution.
causal_claim.evidence_span: At lower drift-field values, the measured spatial resolution is relatively poor because of the combined effects of lower effective detector gain, lower electron drift velocity, and larger transverse diffusion in the drift region. With increasing drift field, the effective gain improves, resulting in better signal formation and more reliable reconstruction of the interaction position.

mechanism_principle.content: Sensitivity enhancement is explained by scattering being stronger for materials with shorter radiation length, especially dense/high-Z matter.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since scattering depends on radiation length and is more pronounced for dense/high-Z materials

mechanism_principle.content: The stabilization effect of conditioning is attributed to moisture removal, residue cleaning, and reduction of surface asperities.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: by removing trapped moisture, cleaning residues and reducing surface asperities which in turn help to suppress micro-discharges and improve long-term gain stability

mechanism_principle.content: Polishing removes asperities and sharp rim features, and ultrasonic cleaning removes residual dust from holes.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: These steps included polishing of the conducting surfaces of the foils with 1200 grit sandpaper initially to remove coarse surface asperities, followed by fine polishing with 2000 grit sandpaper to achieve improved smoothness. Subsequently, buffing was performed using polishing paste to smoothen the copper edges and reduce sharp features around the hole rims. Following the mechanical treatment, the THGEM foils were cleaned in an ultrasonic bath containing a low-foaming, non-ionic detergent for 1 hr to remove residual dust, particularly from within the holes.

mechanism_principle.content: Electron multiplication occurs because primary electrons drift into THGEM holes and undergo secondary ionization in the intense field; the induction field pulls the avalanche to the anode.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Upon entering the gaseous volume, an X-ray photon produced primary electrons in the drift gap through ionization of gaseous molecules, and the electrons drifted towards the THGEM foil under the action of the applied field. Eventually, the electrons underwent multiplication within the holes of the foil through further secondary ionization processes caused by the intense electric field existing across the foil. The field in the induction gap then pulled the electronic avalanche towards the anode which gave rise to a signal.

mechanism_principle.content: Because the Townsend coefficient depends on hole electric field and total ionization varies exponentially with it, gain vs voltage is approximately linear on a log scale.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: As the first Townsend coefficient, α, depends on the electric field inside the THGEM foil holes, and the total ionization varies exponentially with the α, an approximately linear trend was observed in the logarithmic plot of gain versus ΔVTHGEM.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher drift field initially improves electron collection into holes, but at too high field focusing worsens and electrons are lost on the top THGEM surface.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: With the increase in the drift field, electron collection into the THGEM holes was initially improved, leading to a rise in the gain. However, at sufficiently high drift fields, the field configuration became less effective in focusing the electrons into the holes, and a fraction of the electrons was lost on the top surface of the THGEM foil, resulting in a drop in the gain.

mechanism_principle.content: The low-field gain rise with induction field is due to more efficient extraction of avalanche electrons and less loss at the bottom electrode.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: due to more efficient extraction of avalanche electrons and reduced loss at the bottom copper electrode.

mechanism_principle.content: In double-stage operation, diffusion spreads charge to more holes, reducing charge density per hole and thus discharge probability.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Due to electron diffusion after the first amplification stage, the second multiplication occurred in a larger number of holes. As a result, the total final charges were distributed among nearby holes, reducing the charge density in each hole which eventually decreased the probability of discharges caused by a large avalanche in a single hole.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher gain yields more avalanche electrons and more charge sharing over strips, which improves center-of-gravity position reconstruction.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since a higher gain produces a larger number of avalanche electrons, resulting in charge sharing over multiple readout strips, it improves thereby the accuracy of the COG method to determine the position reconstruction.

mechanism_principle.content: Excellent resolution is attributed to high signal-to-noise ratio, effective charge sharing, and center-of-gravity sub-strip interpolation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The excellent position resolution achieved in this work can be attributed to the high signal-to-noise ratio, with electronic noise remaining below 40 ADC channels, as well as effective charge sharing among multiple readout strips. The event positions were reconstructed using the Centre-of-Gravity (CoG) method, which enables sub-strip spatial interpolation and improves localization accuracy.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher drift field improves gain and drift velocity, reducing transverse diffusion time and improving spatial resolution; gain loss at high field is compensated by diffusion/velocity effects.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At the same time, the higher drift velocity reduces the time available for transverse diffusion, which further improves the spatial resolution. Although loss of electrons on the top surface of THGEM at higher drift fields leads to some reduction in detector gain, the spatial resolution remains largely unaffected as the combined effect of transverse diffusion and electron drift velocity compensate for this effect

mechanism_principle.content: Improved discharge tolerance is explained by amplification being distributed over two stages.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
due to the distributed amplification across
two stages.

mechanism_principle.content: The better low-gain resolution of Ar–CO2 is attributed to lower transverse diffusion and higher drift velocity.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
consistent
with its lower transverse diffusion and higher drift-velocity.

hypothesis_statement.content: THGEMs were developed to improve mechanical stability and manufacturing simplicity without sacrificing performance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: THGEMs have been developed to enhance mechanical stability and simplify man- ufacturing, without compromising performance [24].

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose that small-scale prototypes with varied foil parameters are an essential first step toward large-area THGEM muography detectors.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: As an initial and essential step toward this goal, we designed and fabricated several small-scale THGEM prototypes using foils with varied design parameters

hypothesis_statement.content: Varying substrate material, thickness, and geometry should enable systematic study of their effects on detector performance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The THGEM foils were intentionally designed and produced with variations in substrate material, thickness, and key geometrical parameters, to allow a systematic investigation of how such choices influence the detector performance, such as the gas gain, stability, discharge probability, etc.

hypothesis_statement.content: Multistage THGEM operation was explored to increase gain while lowering discharge probability.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To increase the gain while reducing the probability of discharge on the detector foil, the multi-stage operation of the THGEM detector was explored.

evidence_result.content: The Alvarez experiment showed that directional muon flux plus tracking can constrain internal density variations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: That experiment demonstrated that directional muon flux measurements, when com- bined with tracking, could constrain density variations inside monumental structures and established a foundation for modern transmission muography.

evidence_result.content: THGEMs can reach gains of 10^4-10^5, with still higher effective gains in cascaded systems.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At the same time THGEMs can achieve gains as high as 104–105 depending on the gas mixture, pressure, and operational conditions [27, 28], while multi-stage cascaded THGEM systems can achieve even higher effective gains with improved discharge sta- bility [29, 30].

evidence_result.content: Earlier work established sub-millimeter spatial resolution for optimized THGEM detectors under laboratory conditions.
evidence_result.evidence_span: establishing that THGEM-based detectors with optimized hole geometry and segmented readout can achieve sub-millimeter spatial resolution under laboratory conditions [35].

evidence_result.content: Cosmic-ray tests of a mini-drift THGEM chamber achieved about 220 μm spatial resolution.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For example, cosmic-ray tests of a mini-drift THGEM chamber reported a spatial resolution of about 220 𝜇m, demonstrating that appropriately configured THGEM-based detectors can provide precise tracking performance [36].

evidence_result.content: Cortesi et al. reported about 0.7 mm FWHM spatial resolution with a THGEM imaging detector using resistive-anode 2D readout.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In another study, Cortesi et al. investigated a THGEM-based imaging detector and reported a spatial resolution of about 0.7 mm FWHM with a resistive-anode 2D readout, further demonstrating the imaging capability of THGEM-based detectors under laboratory conditions [37].

evidence_result.content: Zhao et al. found reduced-hole/pitch THGEMs achieved position resolution near 75 μm for muon tracking and imaging.
evidence_result.evidence_span: More recently, Zhao et al. developed and studied THGEMs with reduced hole and pitch sizes of few 100s of micron, which were found to have sufficiently good position resolution (close to 75 𝜇m ) for muon tracking and imaging [38].

evidence_result.content: After phase-I, THGEM-A and THGEM-C broke down below 80% of the expected Paschen limit, while THGEM-B reached 96% of the limit.
evidence_result.evidence_span: Initially at this stage, the foils THGEM-A and THGEM-C exhibited breakdown at ΔVTHGEM, below the expected Paschen limit (< 80%), while THGEM-B could reach upto 96% of the limit.

evidence_result.content: Despite oxidation, detector performance was not harmed and the maximum applicable THGEM voltage in UHP nitrogen improved.
evidence_result.evidence_span: However, this did not affect the overall performance of the detectors, rather improved the maximum limit of the applicable ΔVTHGEM in UHP nitrogen.

evidence_result.evidence_span: It shows that the gain reduced at a given ΔVTHGEM due to phase-II conditioning, nevertheless, the working regime could be extended beyond ΔVTHGEM = 1220 V which was the limit in pre-polishing stage.

evidence_result.content: Double-stage gain increased exponentially with bottom-stage voltage, reaching about 33,000 at top voltage 1050 V.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For both the cases of fixed ΔVTop, an exponential increase in gain was observed as the ΔVBottom was raised. A maximum value of gain around 33,000 could be achieved with ΔVTop = 1050 V

constraint.content: Muonography detectors should be robust, have large acceptance, good spatial resolution, high efficiency for minimum-ionizing particles, and stable long-term operation.
constraint.evidence_span: Typical requirements include robust detector design, large geometric accep- tance, good spatial resolution to enable accurate track reconstruction, high detection efficiency for minimum-ionizing particles, and stable long-term operation [9].

constraint.content: Field-deployed muography systems also require robustness, scalability, and cost-effectiveness over long data-taking periods.
constraint.evidence_span: Since many muography deployments involve extended data-taking periods in non-laboratory environments, detector robustness, scalability, and cost-effectiveness are often as critical as intrinsic performance [10].

constraint.content: Foils were prepared to withstand high voltage up to the Paschen limit in ultra-high-purity nitrogen.
constraint.evidence_span: A series of cleaning and conditioning procedures was followed to prepare the foils for application of high voltage across the conducting surfaces with an objective of attaining the Paschen limit in ultra-high purity (UHP) nitrogen.

constraint.content: Efficiency setup required optimized scintillator-detector spacing to maximize angular acceptance.
constraint.evidence_span: To maximize the angular acceptance which requires optimized distances between the scintillators and the detector planes, a Perspex-made test chamber with a height of 42 mm was used to house the THGEM detector.

problem_motivation.content: Developing large-area THGEM detector foils is a critical requirement for realizing a THGEM-based muography system.
evidence_spans: In order to realize a muography system based on THGEM technology, the development of large-area detector foils is a critical requirement.

prior_approach.content: Muon tomography infers internal density variations using naturally occurring cosmic-ray muons.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Muon tomography, often termed as muography, exploits this property to infer on internal density variations in large or shielded structures without using artificial radiation sources.

prior_approach.content: Early muon absorption measurements, especially Alvarez's pyramid study, established transmission muography.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The historical origin of muon tomography or muography is often traced back to early absorp- tion measurements for overburden studies and, most notably, to the pioneering work by Alvarez and collaborators who used cosmic muon absorption to search for hidden chambers in the Pyramid of Khafre [1].

prior_approach.content: Transmission muography measures directional attenuation relative to open-sky flux to reconstruct opacity.
prior_approach.evidence_span: In transmission (attenuation) muography, one measures the directional reduction of muon flux through a target relative to open-sky expectations and reconstructs the integrated density (“opacity”) along each line of sight.

prior_approach.content: Scattering muography uses muon angular deflection from multiple Coulomb scattering.
prior_approach.evidence_span: A second major class is scattering muography, which uses the angular deflection of muons caused by multiple-Coulomb-scattering (MCS) as they traverse matter [6].

prior_approach.content: Various detector technologies have previously been explored for muography.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Consequently, a wide range of detector technologies were explored for muography, including plastic scintilla- tors [11, 12], drift tubes and drift chambers [13, 14], resistive plate chambers (RPCs) [15–17], nuclear emulsions [18], and micro-pattern gaseous detectors (MPGDs) [19–22].

prior_approach.content: Prior studies systematically examined how THGEM geometry affects gain, stability, and discharge probability.
prior_approach.evidence_span: Systematic studies have been carried out to investigate the dependence of gain, stability, and discharge probability on geometrical parameters such as hole diameter, pitch, sub- strate thickness, and rim etching [26, 27].

prior_approach.content: Prior work also studied charging-up, gain uniformity, and long-term stability under irradiation.
prior_approach.evidence_span: The effects of charging-up [31], gain uniformity [32], and long-term stability under sustained irradiation have also been examined, providing important insights into operational behavior relevant for prolonged data-taking scenarios.

prior_approach.content: THGEM operation has previously been demonstrated across multiple gas mixtures and pressures.
prior_approach.evidence_span: THGEM operation has been demonstrated in a variety of gas mixtures and pressures, highlighting the flexibility of the technology and its adaptability to different experimental conditions [33, 34].

inspiration_source.evidence_span: Initially inspired by the concept of GEM, introduced by F. Sauli in 1997 [23], THGEMs have been developed to enhance mechanical stability and simplify man- ufacturing, without compromising performance [24].

causal_claim.content: Greater scattering in dense or high-Z materials gives scattering muography better sensitivity to compact high-Z objects behind lower-Z shielding.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Since scattering depends on radiation length and is more pronounced for dense/high-Z materials, scattering muography provides enhanced sensitivity to compact high-Z objects even when they are shielded by lower-Z materials, making it attractive for security screening and safeguards [7, 8].

causal_claim.content: Fine granularity, flexible geometry, and modern electronics compatibility have driven increased interest in MPGDs.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Among these, MPGDs have attracted increasing attention due to their fine granularity, flexible detector geometry, and compatibility with modern readout electronics.

causal_claim.content: Excellent tracking performance in other applications motivated consideration of GEMs and Micromegas for muography.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Gas Electron Multipliers (GEMs) and Micromegas have demonstrated excellent tracking performance in high-energy physics and related applications, motivating their consideration for muography systems.

causal_claim.content: Conditioning stabilizes THGEM operation and suppresses micro-discharges while improving long-term gain stability.
causal_claim.evidence_span: These conditioning procedures play a crucial role in stabilizing detector operation by removing trapped moisture, cleaning residues and reducing surface asperities which in turn help to suppress micro-discharges and improve long-term gain stability.

causal_claim.content: A best-performing foil was selected based on measured gains over different electric-field configurations.
causal_claim.evidence_span: On the basis of measured gains over a range of electric-field configurations, the prototype with the best-performing foil was subjected to further investigations.

causal_claim.content: Etched rims were used to reduce electrical discharges caused by high applied voltages on THGEM surfaces.
causal_claim.evidence_span: To mitigate the occurrence of electrical discharges caused by high voltages, applied to the conducting surfaces on either sides of the THGEM foil, rims of widths 50 and 100 𝜇m were etched around each hole through standard chemical processes.

causal_claim.content: Phase-II polishing/cleaning was used to reduce discharge probability and enable reaching the Paschen limit.
causal_claim.evidence_span: To reduce the discharge probability and achieve the Paschen limit, a systematic polishing and cleaning procedure for those two THGEM foils (A, and C) was adopted in phase-II.

causal_claim.evidence_span: The ENIG surface-finish, originally applied by the manufacturer, was removed during the polishing of the foils in phase-II. As a result, some surface oxidation occurred on the bare copper electrodes during high-temperature baking due to exposure to the atmosphere

causal_claim.content: Extending the operating regime after phase-II enabled a three-fold gain enhancement.
causal_claim.evidence_span: As a result, three-fold enhancement in the gain value could be achieved.

causal_claim.content: Operating gas choice affects amplification, stability, and spatial resolution.
causal_claim.evidence_span: Since the choice of operating gas significantly impacts charge amplification, operational stability, and spatial resolution, the detector performance was studied using two different Argon-based gas mixtures at atmospheric pressure

causal_claim.content: Average hit multiplicity increased with detector gain, especially in double-stage Ar-isobutane at high gain.
causal_claim.evidence_span: It shows that that the multiplicity increases with the gain and for the double-stage configuration, a fairly large multiplicity can be observed with Ar-isobutane (95:5) at higher gain.

causal_claim.content: In single-stage operation, position resolution improved as gain increased.
causal_claim.evidence_span: In case of single-stage THGEM operation using Ar–CO2 (90:10), a clear improvement was observed with increase in the detector gain.

mechanism_principle.content: Sensitivity enhancement is explained by scattering being stronger for materials with shorter radiation length, especially dense/high-Z matter.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since scattering depends on radiation length and is more pronounced for dense/high-Z materials

mechanism_principle.content: The stabilization effect of conditioning is attributed to moisture removal, residue cleaning, and reduction of surface asperities.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: by removing trapped moisture, cleaning residues and reducing surface asperities which in turn help to suppress micro-discharges and improve long-term gain stability

mechanism_principle.content: Polishing removes asperities and sharp rim features, and ultrasonic cleaning removes residual dust from holes.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: These steps included polishing of the conducting surfaces of the foils with 1200 grit sandpaper initially to remove coarse surface asperities, followed by fine polishing with 2000 grit sandpaper to achieve improved smoothness. Subsequently, buffing was performed using polishing paste to smoothen the copper edges and reduce sharp features around the hole rims. Following the mechanical treatment, the THGEM foils were cleaned in an ultrasonic bath containing a low-foaming, non-ionic detergent for 1 hr to remove residual dust, particularly from within the holes.

mechanism_principle.content: Electron multiplication occurs because primary electrons drift into THGEM holes and undergo secondary ionization in the intense field; the induction field pulls the avalanche to the anode.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Upon entering the gaseous volume, an X-ray photon produced primary electrons in the drift gap through ionization of gaseous molecules, and the electrons drifted towards the THGEM foil under the action of the applied field. Eventually, the electrons underwent multiplication within the holes of the foil through further secondary ionization processes caused by the intense electric field existing across the foil. The field in the induction gap then pulled the electronic avalanche towards the anode which gave rise to a signal.

mechanism_principle.content: Because the Townsend coefficient depends on hole electric field and total ionization varies exponentially with it, gain vs voltage is approximately linear on a log scale.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: As the first Townsend coefficient, α, depends on the electric field inside the THGEM foil holes, and the total ionization varies exponentially with the α, an approximately linear trend was observed in the logarithmic plot of gain versus ΔVTHGEM.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher drift field initially improves electron collection into holes, but at too high field focusing worsens and electrons are lost on the top THGEM surface.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: With the increase in the drift field, electron collection into the THGEM holes was initially improved, leading to a rise in the gain. However, at sufficiently high drift fields, the field configuration became less effective in focusing the electrons into the holes, and a fraction of the electrons was lost on the top surface of the THGEM foil, resulting in a drop in the gain.

mechanism_principle.content: The low-field gain rise with induction field is due to more efficient extraction of avalanche electrons and less loss at the bottom electrode.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: due to more efficient extraction of avalanche electrons and reduced loss at the bottom copper electrode.

mechanism_principle.content: In double-stage operation, diffusion spreads charge to more holes, reducing charge density per hole and thus discharge probability.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Due to electron diffusion after the first amplification stage, the second multiplication occurred in a larger number of holes. As a result, the total final charges were distributed among nearby holes, reducing the charge density in each hole which eventually decreased the probability of discharges caused by a large avalanche in a single hole.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher gain yields more avalanche electrons and more charge sharing over strips, which improves center-of-gravity position reconstruction.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: Since a higher gain produces a larger number of avalanche electrons, resulting in charge sharing over multiple readout strips, it improves thereby the accuracy of the COG method to determine the position reconstruction.

mechanism_principle.content: Excellent resolution is attributed to high signal-to-noise ratio, effective charge sharing, and center-of-gravity sub-strip interpolation.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: The excellent position resolution achieved in this work can be attributed to the high signal-to-noise ratio, with electronic noise remaining below 40 ADC channels, as well as effective charge sharing among multiple readout strips. The event positions were reconstructed using the Centre-of-Gravity (CoG) method, which enables sub-strip spatial interpolation and improves localization accuracy.

mechanism_principle.content: Higher drift field improves gain and drift velocity, reducing transverse diffusion time and improving spatial resolution; gain loss at high field is compensated by diffusion/velocity effects.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span: At the same time, the higher drift velocity reduces the time available for transverse diffusion, which further improves the spatial resolution. Although loss of electrons on the top surface of THGEM at higher drift fields leads to some reduction in detector gain, the spatial resolution remains largely unaffected as the combined effect of transverse diffusion and electron drift velocity compensate for this effect

mechanism_principle.content: Improved discharge tolerance is explained by amplification being distributed over two stages.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
due to the distributed amplification across
two stages.

mechanism_principle.content: The better low-gain resolution of Ar–CO2 is attributed to lower transverse diffusion and higher drift velocity.
mechanism_principle.evidence_span:
consistent
with its lower transverse diffusion and higher drift-velocity.

hypothesis_statement.content: THGEMs were developed to improve mechanical stability and manufacturing simplicity without sacrificing performance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: THGEMs have been developed to enhance mechanical stability and simplify man- ufacturing, without compromising performance [24].

hypothesis_statement.content: The authors propose that small-scale prototypes with varied foil parameters are an essential first step toward large-area THGEM muography detectors.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: As an initial and essential step toward this goal, we designed and fabricated several small-scale THGEM prototypes using foils with varied design parameters

hypothesis_statement.content: Varying substrate material, thickness, and geometry should enable systematic study of their effects on detector performance.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: The THGEM foils were intentionally designed and produced with variations in substrate material, thickness, and key geometrical parameters, to allow a systematic investigation of how such choices influence the detector performance, such as the gas gain, stability, discharge probability, etc.

hypothesis_statement.content: Multistage THGEM operation was explored to increase gain while lowering discharge probability.
hypothesis_statement.evidence_span: To increase the gain while reducing the probability of discharge on the detector foil, the multi-stage operation of the THGEM detector was explored.

evidence_result.content: The Alvarez experiment showed that directional muon flux plus tracking can constrain internal density variations.
evidence_result.evidence_span: That experiment demonstrated that directional muon flux measurements, when com- bined with tracking, could constrain density variations inside monumental structures and established a foundation for modern transmission muography.

evidence_result.content: THGEMs can reach gains of 10^4-10^5, with still higher effective gains in cascaded systems.
evidence_result.evidence_span: At the same time THGEMs can achieve gains as high as 104–105 depending on the gas mixture, pressure, and operational conditions [27, 28], while multi-stage cascaded THGEM systems can achieve even higher effective gains with improved discharge sta- bility [29, 30].

evidence_result.content: Earlier work established sub-millimeter spatial resolution for optimized THGEM detectors under laboratory conditions.
evidence_result.evidence_span: establishing that THGEM-based detectors with optimized hole geometry and segmented readout can achieve sub-millimeter spatial resolution under laboratory conditions [35].

evidence_result.content: Cosmic-ray tests of a mini-drift THGEM chamber achieved about 220 μm spatial resolution.
evidence_result.evidence_span: For example, cosmic-ray tests of a mini-drift THGEM chamber reported a spatial resolution of about 220 𝜇m, demonstrating that appropriately configured THGEM-based detectors can provide precise tracking performance [36].

evidence_result.content: Cortesi et al. reported about 0.7 mm FWHM spatial resolution with a THGEM imaging detector using resistive-anode 2D readout.
evidence_result.evidence_span: In another study, Cortesi et al. investigated a THGEM-based imaging detector and reported a spatial resolution of about 0.7 mm FWHM with a resistive-anode 2D readout, further demonstrating the imaging capability of THGEM-based detectors under laboratory conditions [37].

evidence_result.content: Zhao et al. found reduced-hole/pitch THGEMs achieved position resolution near 75 μm for muon tracking and imaging.
evidence_result.evidence_span: More recently, Zhao et al. developed and studied THGEMs with reduced hole and pitch sizes of few 100s of micron, which were found to have sufficiently good position resolution (close to 75 𝜇m ) for muon tracking and imaging [38].

evidence_result.content: After phase-I, THGEM-A and THGEM-C broke down below 80% of the expected Paschen limit, while THGEM-B reached 96% of the limit.

constraint.content: Muonography detectors should be robust, have large acceptance, good spatial resolution, high efficiency for minimum-ionizing particles, and stable long-term operation.
constraint.evidence_span: Typical requirements include robust detector design, large geometric accep- tance, good spatial resolution to enable accurate track reconstruction, high detection efficiency for minimum-ionizing particles, and stable long-term operation [9].

constraint.content: Field-deployed muography systems also require robustness, scalability, and cost-effectiveness over long data-taking periods.
constraint.evidence_span: Since many muography deployments involve extended data-taking periods in non-laboratory environments, detector robustness, scalability, and cost-effectiveness are often as critical as intrinsic performance [10].

constraint.content: Foils were prepared to withstand high voltage up to the Paschen limit in ultra-high-purity nitrogen.
constraint.evidence_span: A series of cleaning and conditioning procedures was followed to prepare the foils for application of high voltage across the conducting surfaces with an objective of attaining the Paschen limit in ultra-high purity (UHP) nitrogen.

constraint.content: Efficiency setup required optimized scintillator-detector spacing to maximize angular acceptance.
constraint.evidence_span: To maximize the angular acceptance which requires optimized distances between the scintillators and the detector planes, a Perspex-made test chamber with a height of 42 mm was used to house the THGEM detector.

constraint.content: A 50 mV threshold was imposed on the THGEM signal to suppress noise.
constraint.evidence_span: Here, a threshold of 50 mV was set to restrict the noise.

constraint.content: A 24-hour interval between voltage settings was maintained to minimize charging-up effects.
constraint.evidence_span: To reduce the effect of foil charging-up, an interval of 24 hrs was maintained between successive voltage settings.

contradiction.content: At a given ADC in the low-gain region, Ar-CO2 gave better spatial resolution than Ar-isobutane, opposite to what one might expect from gain alone.
contradiction.evidence_span: It was also observed that in the low-gain region, for a given ADC value, the detector provided better spatial resolution in Ar-CO2 (90:10) in comparison to that obtained using Ar-isobutane (95:5).

contradiction.content: Ar–CO2 gave better low-gain spatial resolution than Ar–isobutane.
